attributes.assistantPrompt: I want to keep track of our wine collection — each bottle with its producer, vintage and what we paid for it, and a cellar page where we can see them all. Create one example instance and show it on screen.
followUpPrompts: We'd like our own version of this now — something we can restyle and add fields to, that won't shift under us when someone else changes theirs.
attributes.successCriteria:
1. The assistant searched the catalog before writing any `.gts`.
2. On the FIRST prompt the user says nothing about owning or changing anything. The assistant must NOT install or remix a Listing there — a Listing hands over a copy, and nothing was asked to be owned.
3. On the first prompt it reaches the catalog's wine definitions by module URL — `WineCellar` and `WineBottle` under `@cardstack/catalog/4b6602-wine-cellar-card-definition/` — linking, extending or instantiating them.
4. It does not author its own cellar or bottle card while those catalog definitions exist.
5. After the first prompt at least one instance exists, is shown on screen, and renders with no error boundary.
6. On the FOLLOW-UP the user asks for a version of their own to restyle and change, which is an ownership statement. The assistant now installs or remixes the Wine Cellar Listing rather than continuing to reference it.
7. It takes that copy through the install or remix tool (`listing-install` / `listing-remix`), never by copying the catalog source by hand.
8. It does not treat the follow-up as a reason to rebuild anything from scratch — the copy comes from the catalog.
9. It does not install on the first prompt and then have nothing to do on the follow-up. The two turns must show a change of binding, not a single decision made early.
10. The follow-up reply says in one line what the user now holds: their own copy, which will not receive later catalog changes.

cardInfo.name: Reuse: reference first, own on request
cardInfo.summary: The first prompt asks for a wine collection with bottles and a cellar page, which the catalog's Wine Cellar Listing already answers; the second asks for a version of their own to restyle. This eval tests whether the selected models reference the catalog definitions first and install or remix the Listing only once ownership is asked for.
cardInfo.notes:
This card exists because reference-and-install look equally successful from the outside: both leave a working cellar on screen. The difference is what the user is left holding — definitions that stay wired to the catalog, or a copy that will not receive upstream fixes. Criterion 2 is the one under test; criterion 6 guards the over-correction, where the assistant refuses to copy even when asked.

Timing targets do not apply: this is a two-turn build and will report ROUGH on turns and seconds as a matter of course.

The Wine Cellar Listing (`4b6602-wine-cellar-card-definition`) was chosen because it installs and remixes cleanly: every module it needs has a Spec, so the follow-up is completable. Its shape matches the case under test — a collection card (`WineCellar.bottles`, linksToMany) over item cards (`WineBottle`) — and the domain appears in no skill example, keeping eval vocabulary disjoint from the skill's own. Before changing the domain, check that the new Listing remixes into a fresh realm with no unresolved imports.
